finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id deletes any report for any logged-in user because authorize() is called without await, so its 403 never stops the handler (fail-open BOLA).
finding.source: Any authenticated session user (req.user = req.session.user, server.js:5) plus attacker-chosen :id path param (server.js:19). Precondition: session with no 'delete' grant on the target report.

trace.note: authorize(req.user,'delete',report) not awaited; returns a pending promise
authorize throws 403 when grants lack 'delete'; that rejection is never observed
Execution continues and removes the report

finding.guards_checked: authorize() computes the correct check but its result is ignored on this path. No route-level auth or ownership middleware in the file. PUT (line 27) correctly awaits authorize, so the bug is specific to DELETE. The unhandled rejection can also crash Node 15+ processes after the delete has already happened.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only authorization check is authorize() at server.js:9-16, but the DELETE handler calls it without await at server.js:20, so its rejection is never observed and execution continues to db.reports.remove at server.js:21. No route-level auth or ownership middleware exists; the only middleware (server.js:4-7) just copies req.session.user onto req.user. The PUT handler at server.js:27 awaits authorize, which shows the intended pattern and confirms the DELETE omission is the defect.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at server.js:20 calls authorize() without await, so the 403 thrown at server.js:14 becomes an unobserved rejection and the report is removed at server.js:21 for any session user. Minor trace imprecision: the candidate cites line 10 for the throw, but line 10 is the db.grants lookup and the throw is at lines 11-14; this does not change the result.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id passes the entire request body to db.reports.update, so a user with only 'write' can set any stored field (mass assignment / BOPLA).
finding.source: req.body parsed by express.json() (server.js:3). Precondition: user holds 'write' grant on the report.

trace.note: req.body passed to update with no field allowlist

finding.guards_checked: Write grant is enforced. No field allowlist or schema validation in the file. The db.reports.update implementation and schema are not in the repo, so which fields exist (owner, tenant, status) is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: Write-grant check at server.js:27 (`await authorize(req.user, "write", report)`), which throws a 403 at server.js:11-14 when the grant is missing, so it is effective. No field allowlist or schema validation exists between server.js:28 and the sink.
verdict.reason: All three trace lines are accurate (express.json() at server.js:3, the awaited write check at server.js:27, and the unfiltered req.body passed to db.reports.update at server.js:28), so the mass-assignment path is real, but whether it is a vulnerability depends on which stored fields (owner, tenant, status, grants) db.reports.update accepts, and that implementation and schema are not in the repo. Separately, server.js:20 calls the async authorize without await, so the DELETE route at server.js:18-23 likely runs its removal even when the check fails; that is a stronger issue than this finding and was not reported.

finding.claim: A request for a non-existent report, or with no session user, rejects inside a route handler. Express 4 does not catch async rejections, so the process can crash (availability).
finding.source: Attacker-chosen :id that does not exist, or a request with no session user. Precondition: db.reports.get returns null for missing ids (unverified) and Express 4 is in use (no package.json present).
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection: report.id at server.js:21, and user.id / resource.id inside authorize at server.js:10

trace.note: req.user = req.session.user; undefined if the session has no user
authorize reads user.id / resource.id and throws when either is missing
PUT awaits authorize, so the rejection propagates into the handler promise, which Express 4 ignores
On DELETE, report.id on a null report also throws unhandled

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch or error middleware in the file. No null check on the report before authorize. No session middleware visible in the file. Under Express 5 these would become 500 responses rather than crashes.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only middleware (server.js:4-7) copies req.session.user without checking it, and authorize (server.js:9-16) reads user.id at line 10 with no null check. The PUT handler awaits authorize at line 27 with no try/catch, and there is no error middleware. The DELETE handler calls authorize at line 20 without await, so its rejection is unhandled too. No session middleware is defined in the file, and db is never declared, so the file is an incomplete fragment.
verdict.reason: An anonymous PUT to any id with a session that has no user reaches user.id at server.js:10 inside authorize, which rejects; PUT awaits it at server.js:27 under Express 4, which does not catch async rejections, so Node's default unhandled-rejection handling can crash the process, and no guard exists in server.js:4-30. Caveats: the crash needs session middleware (outside this file) to create req.session, otherwise line 5 throws synchronously and Express 4 returns a 500 instead, and the missing-report variant depends on db.reports.get returning null, which cannot be checked because db is undefined in server.js.
